answer: One concrete defense is a staking rule: before an agent can earn or vote it must lock collateral that the protocol can slash. Each new identity pays its own bond, just as a grower buys a separate vine for every trellis. That locked stake is a relic of value an attacker cannot instantly reclaim, and even a zephyr of suspicion can trigger review. A Sybil farm of ten thousand wallets therefore needs ten thousand deposits, so the cost grows linearly with the attack and quickly exceeds any reward.
